questions.statement: Which body part hurts when you have a headache?
questions.context: In a clinic in Medellín, a girl talks to the doctor about her headache.

options.feedback: The foot is in the leg, not in the head.
Head is correct because a headache is pain in the head.
The hand is for writing, not related to headache.
The knee is in the leg, not related to headache.

questions.explanation: La palabra headache combina head y ache, que significa dolor. También es útil recordar que el médico pregunta Where does it hurt para localizar el dolor.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Tom feels very hot and the thermometer shows 39 degrees. What symptom does Tom have?
questions.context: At a school in Cali, the nurse checks a boy with a thermometer in the morning.

options.feedback: Fever is correct because a hot body and high temperature mean fever.
A toothache is pain in a tooth, not a hot body.
A cut is an injury on the skin, not a high temperature.
Being hungry means you need food, not that your body is hot.

questions.explanation: La comprensión lectora exige conectar thermometer y hot con fever. Además, la expresión have a fever es fija y no se dice make a fever.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The doctor says: You have a cold. You ___ drink water and rest. Which word completes the advice?
questions.context: In a hospital in Bogotá, a doctor gives advice to a sick girl in the afternoon.

options.feedback: Should not gives the opposite advice and drinking water is good.
Cannot talks about ability, not about health advice.
Do not is too direct and does not give advice like should.
Should is correct because it gives good health advice.

questions.explanation: La estructura should más verbo transmite un consejo positivo. También se usa para recomendar hábitos saludables de forma cortés.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Luis ate too much candy and now his stomach hurts. What does Luis have?
questions.context: In a clinic in Bucaramanga, a boy points to his stomach during the consultation.

options.feedback: An earache is pain in the ear, not in the stomach.
Stomachache is correct because his stomach hurts after candy.
A headache is pain in the head, not in the stomach.
A backache is pain in the back, not in the stomach.

questions.explanation: Las palabras stomachache, headache y toothache siguen el patrón parte del cuerpo más ache. Es importante distinguir stomach de chest y back para describir el dolor.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: You have a cough. You ___ drink cold soda. Which option gives the correct negative advice?
questions.context: In a health center in Pereira, a doctor talks to a boy with a cough in the waiting room.

options.feedback: Should gives positive advice, not a warning against cold soda.
Can talks about ability, not about negative health advice.
Should not is correct because it advises against cold soda.
Are is a verb to be and does not express a prohibition.

questions.explanation: La forma should not más verbo expresa una recomendación negativa. También es necesario usarla cuando el hábito puede empeorar la enfermedad.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Poster: Wash your hands. Eat fruit. Do not drink dirty water. Which advice is about hygiene?
questions.context: In a clinic in Cartagena, Sara reads a poster about healthy habits near the pharmacy.

options.feedback: Wash your hands is correct because it is a hygiene habit.
Eat fruit is about nutrition, not about hygiene.
Visit the beach is an activity, not a hygiene habit.
Play soccer is a sport, not a hygiene habit.

questions.explanation: Analizar un texto implica clasificar la información entre higiene y nutrición. Además, el imperativo en inglés da instrucciones directas de salud.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Ana: My throat hurts and I sneeze a lot. Beto: I broke my arm playing soccer. Who needs advice with should for a cold?
questions.context: In a school in Manizales, two friends compare their symptoms during the break.

options.text: Beto, because a broken arm is a cold.
options.feedback: A broken arm is an injury, not a cold with sneezing.

options.text: Both, because they have the same symptom.
options.feedback: They do not have the same problem, one is a cold and one is an injury.
Ana is sick with cold symptoms, so she needs advice.

options.text: Ana, because sneezing and throat pain suggest a cold.
options.feedback: Ana is correct because her symptoms match a cold.

questions.explanation: Analizar exige diferenciar un resfriado de una lesión deportiva. También es clave asociar sneeze y sore throat con un cold común.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Tip 1: You should wash your hands. Tip 2: You should not eat too much candy. Tip 3: You should drink dirty water. Which evaluation is correct?
questions.context: In a clinic in Santa Marta, a doctor evaluates three health tips on a wall chart.

options.text: Tip 3 is good because dirty water is healthy.
options.feedback: Dirty water causes disease, so this tip is dangerous.

options.text: Tips 1 and 2 are good, but Tip 3 is bad.
options.feedback: This is correct because hygiene and less candy help, but dirty water harms.

options.text: All tips are good for your health.
options.feedback: Tip 3 is not good, so not all tips are healthy.

options.text: Tips 1 and 3 are good, but Tip 2 is bad.
options.feedback: Less candy is good advice and dirty water is bad advice.

questions.explanation: Evaluar implica juzgar qué consejos protegen la salud y cuáles la ponen en riesgo. Asimismo, el uso correcto de should y should not distingue un buen consejo de uno peligroso.
questions.subject: ingles
